verdict.rationale: Clerk documents default admin/member Roles plus custom Roles and fine-grained Permissions. It also says each session carries the Organization context (memberships, Roles, Active Organization), and eve tool calls can be gated against the caller's Clerk permissions. However, Roles and Permissions are scoped to Organizations, and a community user reports there is no user-level or global role without falling back to metadata. The docs also never explicitly state that roles and permissions appear as claims in the session JWT, or how backend enforcement works outside eve. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of role/permission claims in the session token, general documented enforcement helpers for authorization checks, and user-level (non-organization) roles.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define roles and permissions and have them enforced and surfaced in session tokens for authorization checks

citations.quote: You can also create custom Roles and fine-grained Permissions that fit your application's specific features and team setup.
Clerk provides the Organization context (memberships, Roles, and the Active Organization) in each session.
This token is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that contains information about the user and their session.
Gate individual eve tool calls against the caller's Clerk permissions and scopes
